In April 2025 we converged on one bill. On April 10, twenty-nine of us said "the save act," and twenty-eight of us said "american voter eligibility" and "in federal elections" the same day. Twenty-seven of us said "safeguard american voter eligibility," "the safeguard american," and "eligibility save act"; twenty-six reached the full "the safeguard american voter eligibility" and "american voter eligibility save act."

The phrase "the save act" first entered the record on 2013-05-15, first said by R000597. The title language — "safeguard american voter eligibility" — first appeared on 2024-05-08, first said by Chip Roy, who also first said "american voter eligibility." "In federal elections" dates to 2015-01-07, first said by Rand Paul.

We record that on a single day our count rose to twenty-nine on one phrase and clustered near twenty-eight on its parts. We said the name of the act, together.
